mainTopic: יעוד of an אמה העבריה: whether it works for a minor son, why it needs consent, and the rulings learned from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: why may a father sell his daughter as a slave after her marriage, if he may not sell her after an earlier slavery? רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the ברייתא allowing it follows רבי אליעזר. Next, ריש לקיש asks whether a master can do יעוד, designating an אמה העבריה as a wife, for his minor son. רבי זירא brings a proof from the פסוק about adultery, and רב אשי pushes it aside. The גמרא then settles the question with רבי ינאי's ruling: יעוד works only with an adult and only with consent. The גמרא gives two ways to explain why the consent is needed. One way ties it to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds that the original sale money was not given for קידושין. The other way, from רב נחמן בר יצחק, learns it straight from the words of the פסוק. Finally, רב נחמן learns two new rulings from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view. A father may tell his minor daughter to accept her own קידושין, and קידושין made with a loan that has a משכון is valid. The explanation of the second ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is selling after marriage really different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends its challenge by asking: is selling a daughter after marriage really different from selling her after slavery?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it different?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge it started just before this point. It asks whether שפחות אחר אישות (slavery after marriage) is really any different from שפחות אחר שפחות (slavery after slavery).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the daughter has already left her father's control. So if he cannot sell her again after an earlier slavery, it seems he also should not be able to sell her after a marriage. The question pushes us to explain why anyone would treat the two cases differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it different? A question that suggests the two cases should be the same

phrases.english: Is it different?
phrases.notes: This finishes a question from just before. It asks if being sold after a marriage is any different from being sold after an earlier slavery.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge from the previous section
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a father may sell his daughter after her marriage even though he may not sell her after her slavery
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In both cases she has fully left her father's authority, so the law should be the same for both

steps.title: How does רב נחמן בר יצחק explain the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the ברייתא that allows selling a daughter after marriage follows, according to רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב נחמן בר יצחק, who says that even according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה the original money was given for קידושין, whose opinion does he say the ברייתא follows?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the opinion of רב נחמן בר יצחק. He holds that even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees the original money was given for קידושין. So the גמרא asks: whose opinion does the ברייתא follow, according to him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the original sale money counts as marriage money, then the girl's sale is tied to marriage. That makes it harder to find a תנא who lets a father sell his daughter after her marriage. So רב נחמן בר יצחק needs another way to explain the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first money, meaning the money paid when she was sold
Was given for the purpose of betrothal
How does he explain it? Whose opinion does it follow?

phrases.english: And according to Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, who says:
Even according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
the original money was given for betrothal,
phrases.notes: This is the money the master first paid the father when he bought the girl.

phrases.english: how does he establish it?
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא that lets a father sell his daughter after she was married.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי מוֹקֵים לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a second אמורא's approach and asks how he explains the same ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the ברייתא follows according to רב נחמן בר יצחק

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the ברייתא according to רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר holds that only slavery after slavery is not allowed, but slavery after marriage is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He explains it according to רבי אליעזר, who says: It is only slavery after slavery that the father cannot sell her into, but he can sell her into slavery after marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who allows שפחות אחר אישות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר makes a split. A father cannot sell his daughter again once she was already sold as a slave. But he can sell her after she was married. This gives רב נחמן בר יצחק a תנא who matches the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Slavery after slavery: selling her again after she was already sold
Slavery after marriage: selling her after she was married, for example as a widow
He is able to sell

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, a father cannot sell his daughter into slavery a second time, but he can sell her after a marriage.

phrases.english: He establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who says:
For slavery after slavery
is when he is not able to sell her,
but for slavery after marriage,
he is able to sell her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹקֵים לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who allows שפחות אחר אישות but not שפחות אחר שפחות

steps.title: Can a father designate a maidservant for his minor son?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks whether a master may do יעוד of an אמה העבריה for his son who is still a קטן. Does the word "his son" in the פסוק mean any son, or only an adult son like the father?
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked: May a man designate a maidservant for his minor son? The Torah says "his son": does that mean any son at all, or a son similar to the father? Just as the father is an adult, so too the son must be an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. ריש לקיש asks a question (a בעיא): can a master do יעוד, designating the maidservant as a wife, for his young son?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שמות says "and if he designates her for his son." One side says "his son" means any son, even a small boy. The other side says the son must be like his father, an adult, since the father himself could have married her.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that has not yet been settled
Designates. The master marks the maidservant as a wife, which makes her married
A minor, a boy who has not yet reached adulthood
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Any at all, whatever kind
Similar to him

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raises a dilemma:
What is the law about a person designating her for his minor son?
The Merciful One said "his son,"
meaning any son at all,
or perhaps his son who is similar to him:
just as he is an adult,
so too, his son must be an adult?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about יעוד for a minor son
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether "his son" in the פסוק of יעוד includes a קטן or only an adult son

steps.title: רבי זירא's proof that a minor has no marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a proof from the פסוק about adultery: a קטן's wife does not count as a married woman. So if יעוד worked for a minor, we would have a marriage for a minor, which the Torah does not recognize.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Come and hear: "A man" comes to exclude a minor. "Who commits adultery with the wife of a man" comes to exclude the wife of a minor. And if you say a father can designate for his minor son, then we would find marriage for a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tries to answer ריש לקיש's question with a תא שמע, a proof. He uses the פסוק about adultery to show that a minor cannot have a real marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that someone who sleeps with a minor's wife is not punished for adultery, because a קטן has no אישות (marriage). If יעוד worked for a minor son, then a minor would have a real marriage. So it seems a father cannot do יעוד for his minor son.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out
Commits adultery
Marriage, the legal state of being married

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate exclusions. "A man" leaves out a minor who commits the act. "The wife of a man" leaves out the wife of a minor. The proof uses the second one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic rule that a קטן cannot have a Torah marriage. That rule decides whether יעוד can work for a young son.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Come and hear:
"A man" excludes a minor.
"Who commits adultery with the wife of a man"
excludes the wife of a minor.
And if you say he can designate,
if so, we find marriage for a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle ריש לקיש's question
steps.raayaObject: That a father cannot do יעוד for his minor son
steps.raayaSupportSource: The derivation from ויקרא 20:10 that the wife of a קטן is not an אשת איש, which shows a minor has no אישות

steps.title: If a minor cannot do יעוד, why does the verse need to exclude him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns רבי זירא's proof around. If a minor's marriage never works, the פסוק would not need to exclude his wife. So maybe the exclusion shows that יעוד does work for a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what are you saying, that he cannot designate? Then why does the פסוק need to exclude a minor? Learn from here that he can designate!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי זירא's proof from the פסוק about adultery. It argues that the proof may actually point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק only needs to exclude something if we might have thought it was included. If a minor could never be married at all, there would be nothing to exclude. So the exclusion suggests there is a way a minor could be married, and the obvious way is יעוד.

keyTerms.meaning: excludes (the פסוק leaves this case out)
resolve the question (from this source)
he can designate (do יעוד of the אמה העבריה)

phrases.english: But rather, what, that he cannot designate?
Then why does the verse exclude him?
phrases.notes: If a minor can never be married, there is no reason to say his wife is left out.

phrases.english: Resolve from it that he can designate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי, אֵינוֹ מְיַיעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's proof (step 5) and argues that it supports the opposite conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's proof that a minor's wife is not a married woman, so יעוד cannot work for a minor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that excludes something implies the case was possible. So the exclusion suggests a minor can sometimes be married, through יעוד.

steps.title: The verse is about a nine-year-old יבם
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the פסוק is needed for a different case: a יבם aged nine years and one day who lived with his יבמה. By Torah law she is fit for him and his relations count, so we might have thought she is fully his wife. The פסוק teaches that she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Here we are dealing with a יבם who is nine years and one day old who lived with his יבמה. By Torah law she is fit for him. You might have thought that since she is fit for him and his relations count, anyone who lives with her is guilty of being with a married woman. So the פסוק teaches us that he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He shows that the פסוק's exclusion has a real case to talk about that has nothing to do with יעוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations of a boy nine years and one day old count legally, and יבום has no minimum age in the Torah. So someone could think the young יבם fully acquires her. The פסוק is needed to exclude this case, so it gives no proof that יעוד works for a minor.

keyTerms.meaning: the brother of a man who died childless, who may marry the widow
his יבמה, the widow of his childless brother
his relations count legally as relations
a married woman
you might have said (sets up the mistaken idea)
it teaches us (the correct idea)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not prove that יעוד works or fails for a minor. He only shows that the פסוק can be explained without it, so רבי זירא's proof does not settle ריש לקיש's question. The גמרא then looks for a direct ruling, which comes in step 9.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּיָבָם בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: Here, with a yavam nine years and one day old
who had relations with his yevama, we are dealing,
since by Torah law she is fit for him.
You might have said:
Since by Torah law she is fit for him
and his relations count as relations,
one who has relations with her is liable for a married woman.
So it teaches us that he is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6 by finding another case for the פסוק's exclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to a different case (a young יבם), so it says nothing about יעוד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the young יבם's relations count by Torah law, she is fully his wife and another man who lives with her is liable for אשת איש.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is not a full אשת איש. The פסוק excludes this case, so its exclusion does not show that יעוד works for a minor.

steps.title: So what is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Since the proofs back and forth did not settle it, the גמרא asks what the final ruling is about יעוד for a minor son.
steps.simpleTranslation: What came of this question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final answer to ריש לקיש's question. This line sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי זירא's proof and the challenge to it have been answered, so the proofs so far do not settle ריש לקיש's question. The גמרא now looks for a direct ruling, which the next step brings.

keyTerms.meaning: what came of it? (what is the final ruling?)

phrases.english: What came of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof and challenge cancel out, the גמרא goes back to ריש לקיש's question from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final ruling on whether a master can do יעוד for his minor son.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: יעוד only with an adult and only with consent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אייבו quotes רבי ינאי: יעוד works only with an adult man, and יעוד works only with consent. So a master cannot do יעוד for his minor son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אייבו said in the name of רבי ינאי: יעוד is only with an adult. יעוד is only with consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי ינאי's ruling as the answer. יעוד does not work for a minor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles ריש לקיש's question: 'his son' in the פסוק means an adult son. רבי ינאי also adds a second rule, that יעוד needs consent, which the גמרא will look at next.

keyTerms.meaning: designating the אמה העבריה as a wife
an adult
with consent (with full awareness)

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling: a master cannot do יעוד for his son who is a קטן. יעוד works only with an adult.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Aivu said that Rabbi Yannai said:
Designation applies only to an adult,
designation applies only with consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8 with a ruling of an אמורא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יעוד works only with an adult man and only with consent, so it does not work for a minor son.

steps.title: Why does רבי ינאי need two rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ינאי says two things. If יעוד needs consent, we already know a minor can't do it, because a minor cannot legally give consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two rules?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of רבי ינאי's statement. It sounds like he said the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor's consent does not count legally. So 'only with consent' already tells us 'only an adult.' The second statement seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: two (why two statements?)

phrases.english: Two?
phrases.notes: The גמרא means that 'with consent' already shows it must be an adult, since a minor's consent does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the double wording of רבי ינאי's ruling from step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Needing consent already rules out a minor, so the statement 'only with an adult' seems repeated for no reason.

steps.title: The second rule is the reason for the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי ינאי is giving one rule with its reason. יעוד works only with an adult because יעוד needs consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is saying 'what is the reason.' Why is יעוד only with an adult? Because יעוד is only with consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two lines are one ruling and its explanation, not two separate rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read the second line as 'because.' The rule is 'adult only,' and the reason is that יעוד needs real consent, which a minor cannot give.

keyTerms.meaning: he is saying 'what is the reason' (the second part explains the first)

phrases.english: He is saying 'what is the reason.'

phrases.aramaic: מָה טַעַם אֵין יִעוּד אֶלָּא בְּגָדוֹל –
phrases.english: What is the reason that designation applies only to an adult?
Because designation applies only with consent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'two rules?' challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the wording: the second clause is the reason for the first, not a separate law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ינאי gave two separate rulings, which repeat each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one ruling with its reason: adult only, because consent is needed.

steps.title: Another answer: 'with consent' means her consent
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: 'with consent' means the woman's consent, so it is a separate rule. This is based on the ברייתא of אביי the son of רבי אבהו, who reads 'אשר לא יעדה' as teaching that he must inform her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: what does 'with consent' mean? With her consent. As אביי the son of רבי אבהו taught: 'Who did not designate her' teaches that he must inform her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer the 'two rules?' challenge. The two rules are about different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, 'only an adult' is about the man, and 'only with consent' is about the woman, so nothing is repeated. The source is a play on the word יעדה, read as if it means 'to inform her,' teaching that she must know and agree.

keyTerms.meaning: or if you wish, say (a second answer)
hers (her own consent)
to inform her (to tell her about the יעוד)

steps.whatToRemember: יעוד needs two things: an adult man, and consent. According to the second answer, the consent is the woman's, based on 'אשר לא יעדה.'

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What is 'with consent'? With her consent.
As Abaye, son of Rabbi Abbahu, taught:
'Who did not designate her'
teaches that he must inform her.
phrases.notes: The word יְעָדָהּ is read as if it says 'inform her,' so she has to know about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מַאי מִדַּעַת – מִדַּעַת דִּידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge in step 10, different from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two clauses between two people: 'adult' refers to the man, 'consent' refers to the woman.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses are about the man, so the second repeats the first.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'With consent' means her consent, a separate requirement learned from 'אשר לא יעדה.'

steps.title: The author explains his own ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי the son of רבי אבהו explains that his ברייתא about informing her follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds the original money was not given for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same person who taught the ברייתא also explained it: it is talking about קידושי יעוד, and it follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who said the first money was not given for קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The person who taught the ברייתא in the last step now explains why the master must inform the girl. He says the ברייתא follows the opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money the master paid to buy her was not given for קידושין, then יעוד is a brand-new קידושין. A new קידושין needs the woman's agreement, so he must tell her.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal through designation, when the master (or his son) designates the maidservant as a wife
The original money, which was paid to buy the maidservant
According to the opinion of

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: He taught it, and he explained it:
phrases.notes: 'He' is אביי the son of רבי אבהו, who taught the ברייתא about informing her in the last step.

phrases.english: It is about betrothal through designation,
and it follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: the original money
was not given for betrothal.
phrases.notes: This is the money the master paid her father when he bought her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the ברייתא quoted in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The requirement to inform her before יעוד follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds the original sale money was not given for קידושין, so יעוד is a new קידושין needing her consent.

steps.title: The rule can hold even if the money was for קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says she must be informed even if the original money was given for קידושין, because the Torah says 'יעדה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Even if you say the money was given for קידושין, this case is different, because the Torah says 'יעדה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another way to explain the ברייתא. He says it does not need to follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the purchase money did count toward קידושין, the Torah's word 'יעדה' teaches that he must still inform her. So the need for her consent comes straight from the פסוק, not from the debate about the money.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say
Here it is different
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
'Designated her', the Torah's word for יעוד

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Even if you say it was given for betrothal,
here it is different, since the Torah says "designated her."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לְקִידּוּשִׁין נִיתְּנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different basis for the same ברייתא, without needing רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative source: the rule comes from the פסוק itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view about the original money
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the other view agrees she must be informed, because the Torah says 'יעדה'

steps.title: Where is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view stated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has mentioned רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view, and now it asks where that view is taught. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to see the actual source where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the original money was not for קידושין. This makes sure we understand the view the ברייתא depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is the teaching of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion cited in step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view about the original money appears

steps.title: The ברייתא: there must be time left for redemption
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'יעדה והפדה' together: יעוד needs enough time left in the day for her to be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'יעדה... והפדה' (designated her... let her be redeemed). So there must be enough time left in the day for redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads two words of the פסוק together. This sets up רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah puts 'designate her' right next to 'let her be redeemed'. So יעוד can only happen at a time when redemption is still possible. On her last day, enough time must be left for her to still be redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Then he shall let her be redeemed'
Enough time
Redemption, buying her freedom

phrases.english: As it is taught: "designated her, then he shall let her be redeemed"

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא שְׁהוּת בַּיּוֹם כְּדֵי פְדִיָּיה.
phrases.english: there must be enough time in the day for redemption.
phrases.notes: This means on the last day of her service, there must still be time left for her to be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״יְעָדָהּ, וְהֶפְדָּהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא that links יעוד to redemption, which leads to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: she needs a פרוטה's worth of time left
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules that the יעוד works only if enough time is left in the day for her to work off a שוה פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: If there is enough time left in the day to do work worth a פרוטה for him, she is betrothed. If not, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns a practical rule from the ברייתא. The יעוד works only if she still owes at least a פרוטה's worth of work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master makes the קידושין with the value of the work she still owes him. If less than a פרוטה's worth of time is left, there is nothing to make the קידושין with, so it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: From here
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest value for קידושין
She is betrothed

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: From here Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda said:
If there is enough time left in the day
to do work for him worth a perutah,
she is betrothed,
and if not, she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical ruling from the ברייתא in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעוד works only if enough time is left for her to do work worth a פרוטה; otherwise she is not betrothed.

steps.title: So he holds the original money was not for קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from his ruling that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds the original money was not given for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that he holds the original money was not given for קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling. This is the answer to 'where is his view?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the purchase money already counted for קידושין, he would not need a פרוטה's worth of remaining work. Since he does need it, the קידושין must come from the remaining work, not from the first money.

keyTerms.meaning: We see from this, apparently
He holds

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
the original money was not given for betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Infers the underlying view from the ruling in step 17
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds the original money was not given for קידושין
steps.raayaSupportSource: His requirement of a פרוטה's worth of remaining time for the קידושין

steps.title: The פסוק 'והפדה' could explain his ruling instead
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ruling does not prove it: even if the money was for קידושין, the Torah links יעוד to 'והפדה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Even if you say the money was given for קידושין, this case is different, because the Torah says 'והפדה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on the conclusion from the last step. He says the ruling could fit even the view that the money was for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The need for time left in the day may come from a Torah rule, not from the money. Because the Torah put 'והפדה' right next to 'יעדה', יעוד must happen while she can still be redeemed, whatever the first money was for.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the rules of יעוד. One says they come from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view that the purchase money was not for קידושין. רב נחמן בר יצחק says they come straight from the words of the פסוק, 'יעדה' and 'והפדה'.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the same opening sentence twice, in step 14 and here. In step 14 he points to the word 'יעדה' to explain why she must be informed. Here he points to 'והפדה' to explain why time must be left in the day.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Even if you say it was given for betrothal,
here it is different, since the Torah says "then he shall let her be redeemed."
phrases.notes: Because 'redeem' sits right next to 'designate' in the פסוק, the designation must happen while she can still be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לְקִידּוּשִׁין נִיתְּנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds the money was not for קידושין; his ruling itself stands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The time requirement can come from the Torah linking 'יעדה' to 'והפדה', so it does not prove anything about the original money

steps.title: A father may tell his minor daughter to accept her own קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב נחמן rules that a father may tell his minor daughter, 'Go out and accept your קידושין,' and he learns this from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: A man may tell his young daughter, 'Go and accept your קידושין.' We learn this from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב נחמן, and he says it comes from the opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that we just learned. The next step will show how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the father is the one who accepts קידושין for his daughter while she is a קטנה. רב נחמן says she can receive the קידושין herself, as long as her father tells her to.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who is still a minor, under the age of מצוות
'Go out and accept your קידושין', the father's instruction to his daughter
'From רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה', meaning the ruling is learned from his opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view on יעוד has practical results for ordinary קידושין too, not only for an אמה עבריה.

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
A person may say to his minor daughter
"Go out and accept your betrothal,"
[we learn this] from Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אוֹמֵר אָדָם לְבִתּוֹ קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה from the earlier steps as a source for a new ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father may tell his minor daughter to accept her own קידושין, and it works.

steps.title: How the daughter's קידושין rule comes from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since the first money for the אמה עבריה was not for קידושין, the קידושין at יעוד comes from the work time left in her. So she is the one who receives the קידושין, and the same is true here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה say that the first money was not given for קידושין, and if there is still a פרוטה's worth of work left in her, it is a valid קידושין? Here too it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב נחמן's ruling about the minor daughter comes from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first money was not קידושין money, then at the time of יעוד the father gets nothing new. The קידושין is the value of the work time left in the girl, so in effect she herself is receiving the קידושין. The same logic lets a minor daughter accept her own קידושין when her father agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: The first money, which the master paid the father when he bought the אמה עבריה
There is still some left in her, meaning time left on her work term
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount of value that counts
Here too it is no different, meaning the same logic applies

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda say
the first money was not given for betrothal,
phrases.notes: This is the money the master paid the father when he bought her as an אמה עבריה.

phrases.english: and when there is still [work] worth a peruta left in her
it is a valid betrothal?
Here too, it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מָעוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת לָאו לְקִידּוּשִׁין נִיתְּנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source for the ruling in step 20
steps.raayaObject: A minor daughter can accept her own קידושין when her father tells her to
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view that the first money was not for קידושין, so the קידושין at יעוד comes from the work time left in the girl herself

steps.title: קידושין with a loan that has collateral is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב נחמן rules that if a man betroths a woman with a loan that has a משכון, she is מקודשת, and he learns this from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: If someone makes קידושין with a loan that has collateral, she is betrothed. We learn this from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from רב נחמן, also learned from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The next step will explain how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, letting a woman off a loan she owes is not good enough for קידושין. רב נחמן says that when the loan has a משכון backing it, the קידושין does work.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes קידושין with a loan, by letting her off a debt she owes him
Collateral, an item given to the lender as a guarantee for the loan
She is betrothed, the קידושין is valid

phrases.english: And Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
One who betroths [a woman] with a loan
phrases.notes: She owes him money, and he lets her off the debt as her קידושין.

phrases.english: that has collateral on it, she is betrothed,
[we learn this] from Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ בְּמִלְוָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ מַשְׁכּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling learned from the same source as step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין made with a loan that has a משכון is valid.

steps.title: The אמה עבריה is like a loan where she herself is the collateral
steps.stepSummary: Since the first money was not for קידושין, the girl's work is like a loan, and she herself is the משכון. Yet יעוד still works, so a loan with a משכון can work for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה say that the first money was not given for קידושין? So this is a loan, and she herself is the collateral.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain how the loan-with-collateral ruling comes from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first money was not קידושין money, it is like a loan that the girl pays back with her work. Her own body serves as the משכון for that loan. Since יעוד still makes a valid קידושין, a loan that has a משכון can also be used for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan
She herself, her own body

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda say
the first money was not given for betrothal?
[So] this is a loan,
phrases.notes: The master's payment is like a loan that she pays back with her work.

phrases.english: and she herself is the collateral,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי הַלְוָאָה הִיא, וְהִיא גּוּפַהּ מַשְׁכּוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source for the ruling in step 22, in the same way step 21 explained step 20
steps.raayaObject: קידושין with a loan that has a משכון is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: In רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view, the אמה עבריה is like a loan with her own body as the משכון, and יעוד still makes a valid קידושין
